title: List connected USB devices
summary: Show every USB device the Linux system currently detects, such as keyboards, mice, flash drives and hubs. The command only reads information and changes nothing.

aliases.text: what usb devices are plugged in

prerequisites: A Linux computer with a terminal window
The lsusb command from the usbutils package (installed by default on most desktop distributions)

steps.explain: List every USB device the kernel currently detects, one per line. Each line shows the bus, device number, vendor:product ID and the device name.
steps.expect: One line per device, like 'Bus 001 Device 002: ID 046d:c52b ...'. Root hub lines are the computer's own USB ports and are always present.

alternatives.explain: Show the same devices as a tree, grouped by hub, so you can see which device is plugged into which hub or port.

verify.expect: The device you plugged in appears as its own line with its name at the end.

source.title: lsusb manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
